citation: Y. Kida, Y. Nakano, K. Motoyoshi and T. Imasaka, "Frequency-resolved optical gating with two nonlinear optical processes", Opt. Lett. 39, 3006-3009 (2014)
readability: PDF text layer extracted (pypdf; the Read tool's PDF renderer was unavailable: pdftoppm not installed). All text read; the figures (traces, retrieved pulses, phases) could NOT be viewed, so retrieved intensities / phases / the chirp magnitude are UNVERIFIED and not used.
topic: double FROG: SHG-FROG of two pulses + XFROG analysed together removes the SHG time-direction ambiguity

referenceNumbers.value: 1200 nm from an OPA; delayed by ~300 fs w.r.t. the reference
5 um thick, phi = 90 deg, theta = 33.2 deg; non-collinear, f = 200 mm concave mirror
referenceNumbers.status: read (type of phase matching not stated)

referenceNumbers.value: 0.5 % (SHG-FROG, all retrievals); XFROG 0.4-0.5 % with the right reference, 0.9-1.0 % with the time-reversed one
SHG (reference) 0.5 %, XFROG 0.4 %, constant over six retrievals; six retrievals identical, no time-reversed replica
SHG(ref) + XFROG only: profiles vary like conventional, time-reversed replica appears randomly

assumptions: Reference: Gaussian, 30 fs transform limit, GDD +195 fs^2 -> 35 fs. Test: Gaussian, 40 fs transform limit, GDD +580 fs^2 before 3 mm fused silica -> 57.6 fs. The paper's retrieved phases (Figs. 4, 5, 7) were not visible; only 'positive chirp' of the test pulse is stated.
Synthetic traces on a 128 x 128 grid (3 fs), additive noise 0.4 % of the peak (chosen a priori as a typical spectrometer noise; the absolute G errors depend on it, only comparisons are made).
XFROG delay range = the same full range as the SHG traces (the paper limits it to one signal at +tau).

The retrieval is written in numpy: generalised projections with PCGPA steps for the SHG traces and a least-squares step for the XFROG (Fig. 6 of the paper); the initial guess is a 40 fs Gaussian with random phase noise (not stated in the paper).
